children.text: The historical GW150914 signal is modelled as two masses M1 and M2 on slowly shrinking, nonrelativistic circular orbits. Positions are relative to their centre of mass, \(M_1\mathbf r_1+M_2\mathbf r_2=0\). Define \(M=M_1+M_2\), \(\mu=M_1M_2/M\), separation L and orbital angular velocity Ω. Use G=\(6.67\times10^{-11}\) N m²/kg², c=\(3.00\times10^{8}\) m/s, solar mass \(2.00\times10^{30}\) kg and solar radius \(7.00\times10^{5}\) km. The given quadrupole radiation formula is \[\mathcal P=\frac{G}{5c^5}\sum_{i,j=1}^3(\dddot Q_{ij})^2,\quad Q_{ij}=\sum_{A=1}^2M_A(x_{Ai}x_{Aj}-\delta_{ij}r_A^2/3).\] The gravitational-wave cycle frequency is twice the orbital cycle frequency. Treat this Newtonian/quadrupole model as the specified approximation, even near merger.
Write \(\ddot{\mathbf r}_1=-\alpha\mathbf r_1/r_1^n\). Find n and α.
Write the energy as \(E=\beta GM\mu/L\). Find β.
Choose mass 1 at \(r_1(\cos\Omega t,\sin\Omega t)\). Write \(Q_{ii}=\mu L^2(a_i+b_i\cos kt)/2\), \(Q_{ij}=\mu L^2c_{ij}\sin kt/2\) for i≠j. Find k and all coefficients.
Use \(\dot E=-\mathcal P\) to obtain \((\dot\Omega)^3=(3\xi)^3\Omega^{11}(GM_c)^5/c^{15}\). Find Mc in terms of M and μ.
Relate Ω to fGW and integrate to show \(f_{GW}^{-8/3}=8\pi^{8/3}\xi(GM_c/c^3)^{2/3+p}(t_0-t)^{2-p}\). Determine p.

statement.text:
LIGO-GW150914
The historical GW150914 signal is modelled as two masses M1 and M2 on slowly shrinking, nonrelativistic circular orbits. Positions are relative to their centre of mass, \(M_1\mathbf r_1+M_2\mathbf r_2=0\). Define \(M=M_1+M_2\), \(\mu=M_1M_2/M\), separation L and orbital angular velocity Ω. Use G=\(6.67\times10^{-11}\) N m²/kg², c=\(3.00\times10^{8}\) m/s, solar mass \(2.00\times10^{30}\) kg and solar radius \(7.00\times10^{5}\) km. The given quadrupole radiation formula is \[\mathcal P=\frac{G}{5c^5}\sum_{i,j=1}^3(\dddot Q_{ij})^2,\quad Q_{ij}=\sum_{A=1}^2M_A(x_{Ai}x_{Aj}-\delta_{ij}r_A^2/3).\] The gravitational-wave cycle frequency is twice the orbital cycle frequency. Treat this Newtonian/quadrupole model as the specified approximation, even near merger.
a.1. Newtonian acceleration
Write \(\ddot{\mathbf r}_1=-\alpha\mathbf r_1/r_1^n\). Find n and α.
a.2. Binary kinetic energy
In \(E=A(\mu,\Omega,L)-GM\mu/L\), find A.
a.3. Circular energy coefficient
Write the energy as \(E=\beta GM\mu/L\). Find β.
b.1. Time-dependent quadrupole
Choose mass 1 at \(r_1(\cos\Omega t,\sin\Omega t)\). Write \(Q_{ii}=\mu L^2(a_i+b_i\cos kt)/2\), \(Q_{ij}=\mu L^2c_{ij}\sin kt/2\) for i≠j. Find k and all coefficients.
b.2. Radiated power coefficient
Find ξ in \(\mathcal P=\xi G\mu^2L^4\Omega^6/c^5\).
b.3. Chirp mass
Use \(\dot E=-\mathcal P\) to obtain \((\dot\Omega)^3=(3\xi)^3\Omega^{11}(GM_c)^5/c^{15}\). Find Mc in terms of M and μ.
b.4. Chirp integration
Relate Ω to fGW and integrate to show \(f_{GW}^{-8/3}=8\pi^{8/3}\xi(GM_c/c^3)^{2/3+p}(t_0-t)^{2-p}\). Determine p.
b.5. Mass from the measured chirp

In the strain graph A,B,C,D occur at t=0.000, 0.009, 0.034, 0.040 s. Estimate fGW at midpoint tAB and tCD, then estimate Mc and total M in solar masses assuming equal component masses.
b.6. Compactness and orbital speed
At tCD estimate minimum separation L, maximum individual radius Rmax, ratio Rsun/Rmax, and individual orbital speed vcol/c.

children.text: \(\mathbf r_2=-(M_1/M_2)\mathbf r_1\), so separation is \((M_1+M_2)r_1/M_2\). Newton's law then gives \(n=3\), \(\alpha=GM_2^3/(M_1+M_2)^2\).
The centre-of-mass identity \(M_1r_1^2+M_2r_2^2=\mu L^2\) gives \(A=\mu L^2\Omega^2/2\).
Force balance gives \(\Omega^2=GM/L^3\). Substitution gives \(E=-GM\mu/(2L)\), so β=−1/2.

The matrix is \[Q=\frac{\mu L^2}{2}\begin{pmatrix}1/3+\cos2\Omega t&\sin2\Omega t&0\\\sin2\Omega t&1/3-\cos2\Omega t&0\\0&0&-2/3\end{pmatrix}.\] Hence k=2Ω, a=(1/3,1/3,−2/3), b=(1,−1,0), c12=c21=1 and all remaining off-diagonal coefficients vanish.
Third derivatives have amplitude \(4\mu L^2\Omega^3\). Summing both diagonal and both off-diagonal contributions gives twice its square. Thus \(\xi=32/5\).
Differentiate \(E=-GM\mu/(2L)\) and \(L^3\Omega^2=GM\) to eliminate L and its derivative. This gives \(\dot\Omega=3\xi G^{5/3}\mu M^{2/3}\Omega^{11/3}/c^5\), hence \(M_c=(\mu^3M^2)^{1/5}\).
Because fGW=2Ω/(2π), Ω=πfGW. Integrating \(\dot\Omega=\chi\Omega^{11/3}\) gives \(\Omega^{-8/3}=(8/3)\chi(t_0-t)\). Therefore \(f_{GW}^{-8/3}=8\pi^{8/3}\xi(GM_c/c^3)^{5/3}(t_0-t)\), so p=1.
b.5. Mass from the measured chirp

The indicated intervals are half-periods: fAB=1/(2×0.009)=55.6 Hz and fCD=1/(2×0.006)=83.3 Hz, at 0.0045 s and 0.037 s. Eliminating t0 between the two integrated chirp equations gives t0≈0.054 s and Mc≈30 solar masses. Equal masses give \(M=4^{3/5}M_c\simeq69\) solar masses. Values depend on graph reading and the stated approximation.

\(\Omega=\pi f_{CD}\simeq262\,\mathrm{rad/s}\), \(L=(GM/\Omega^2)^{1/3}\simeq500\,\mathrm{km}\). Non-overlap implies Rmax≈L/2≈250 km, so Rsun/Rmax≈3000. Each equal mass moves at \(v=\Omega L/2\simeq7\times10^4\,\mathrm{km/s}\simeq0.2c\). These large speeds also expose the limits of the nonrelativistic model.

solution.text:
LIGO-GW150914
a.1. Newtonian acceleration
\(\mathbf r_2=-(M_1/M_2)\mathbf r_1\), so separation is \((M_1+M_2)r_1/M_2\). Newton's law then gives \(n=3\), \(\alpha=GM_2^3/(M_1+M_2)^2\).
a.2. Binary kinetic energy
The centre-of-mass identity \(M_1r_1^2+M_2r_2^2=\mu L^2\) gives \(A=\mu L^2\Omega^2/2\).
a.3. Circular energy coefficient
Force balance gives \(\Omega^2=GM/L^3\). Substitution gives \(E=-GM\mu/(2L)\), so β=−1/2.
b.1. Time-dependent quadrupole
The matrix is \[Q=\frac{\mu L^2}{2}\begin{pmatrix}1/3+\cos2\Omega t&\sin2\Omega t&0\\\sin2\Omega t&1/3-\cos2\Omega t&0\\0&0&-2/3\end{pmatrix}.\] Hence k=2Ω, a=(1/3,1/3,−2/3), b=(1,−1,0), c12=c21=1 and all remaining off-diagonal coefficients vanish.
b.2. Radiated power coefficient
Third derivatives have amplitude \(4\mu L^2\Omega^3\). Summing both diagonal and both off-diagonal contributions gives twice its square. Thus \(\xi=32/5\).
b.3. Chirp mass
Differentiate \(E=-GM\mu/(2L)\) and \(L^3\Omega^2=GM\) to eliminate L and its derivative. This gives \(\dot\Omega=3\xi G^{5/3}\mu M^{2/3}\Omega^{11/3}/c^5\), hence \(M_c=(\mu^3M^2)^{1/5}\).
b.4. Chirp integration
Because fGW=2Ω/(2π), Ω=πfGW. Integrating \(\dot\Omega=\chi\Omega^{11/3}\) gives \(\Omega^{-8/3}=(8/3)\chi(t_0-t)\). Therefore \(f_{GW}^{-8/3}=8\pi^{8/3}\xi(GM_c/c^3)^{5/3}(t_0-t)\), so p=1.
b.5. Mass from the measured chirp
The indicated intervals are half-periods: fAB=1/(2×0.009)=55.6 Hz and fCD=1/(2×0.006)=83.3 Hz, at 0.0045 s and 0.037 s. Eliminating t0 between the two integrated chirp equations gives t0≈0.054 s and Mc≈30 solar masses. Equal masses give \(M=4^{3/5}M_c\simeq69\) solar masses. Values depend on graph reading and the stated approximation.
b.6. Compactness and orbital speed
\(\Omega=\pi f_{CD}\simeq262\,\mathrm{rad/s}\), \(L=(GM/\Omega^2)^{1/3}\simeq500\,\mathrm{km}\). Non-overlap implies Rmax≈L/2≈250 km, so Rsun/Rmax≈3000. Each equal mass moves at \(v=\Omega L/2\simeq7\times10^4\,\mathrm{km/s}\simeq0.2c\). These large speeds also expose the limits of the nonrelativistic model.
